`D3.js` can draw almost any chart, but it has a steep learning curve and asks for some `HTML`, `CSS` and `JavaScript`. `ddplot` wraps a collection of `D3` charts in plain `R` functions: you pass a data frame and column names, and you get an interactive SVG graphic that works in the RStudio viewer, R Markdown, Quarto and Shiny.

`ddplot` is built on the [r2d3](https://rstudio.github.io/r2d3/) package, which does the heavy lifting of connecting `R` and `D3`. Thanks to its developers.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# From CRAN
install.packages("ddplot")

# Development version from GitHub
remotes::install_github("feddelegrand7/ddplot")
```

```{r setup}
library(ddplot)
```

## Your first charts

Every function takes a data frame and the names of the columns to plot, as strings.

### A time series

`line_chart()` accepts a `ts` object directly. Hover over the chart to read the values, drag on it to zoom, or use the range buttons and the navigator below it:

```{r}
line_chart(AirPassengers, y = "passengers", title = "Airline passengers, 1949-1960")
```

A multivariate `ts` gives one line per column. With a data frame, give the date column as `x` and one or several value columns as `y` (or a single value column and a `group` column):

```{r}
line_chart(
  EuStockMarkets,
  transform = "index",
  title = "European stock indices",
  subtitle = "Rebased to 100 at the first visible date; zoom in to move the base"
)
```

### Comparing categories

Bar charts expect one row per category. Aggregate first, for instance with `dplyr`:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2) # for the mpg data

mpg %>%
  group_by(manufacturer) %>%
  summarise(mean_cty = mean(cty)) %>%
  bar_chart(
    x = "manufacturer",
    y = "mean_cty",
    sort = "descending",
    fill = "#4269d0",
    ytitle = "Average city miles per gallon",
    title = "City fuel economy by manufacturer"
  )
```

### A relationship

```{r}
scatter_plot(
  data = mpg,
  x = "displ",
  y = "hwy",
  col = "#4269d0",
  size = 4,
  xtitle = "Engine displacement (litres)",
  ytitle = "Highway miles per gallon",
  title = "Bigger engines, fewer miles"
)
```

## Arguments shared by most charts

The functions share a common vocabulary, so what you learn on one chart carries over to the others:

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `data`, `x`, `y` | The data frame and the columns to plot, given as strings |
| `title`, `titleFontSize` | Chart title and its size in pixels |
| `xtitle`, `ytitle` | Axis titles |
| `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `col` | Colours and outlines of the marks |
| `bgcol`, `axisCol` | Background and axis colours |
| `font` | Font family, for example `"Georgia, serif"` |
| `xticks`, `yticks` | Approximate number of ticks on each axis |
| `width`, `height` | Size of the widget, passed to `r2d3::r2d3()` |

Each function's help page lists its full set of options, for example `?line_chart`.

## Find the right chart

`ddplot` has more than 40 chart types. The [gallery](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/gallery.html) shows all of them, and the guides below walk through each one with examples, starting with the charts you are most likely to need:

| Guide | Charts |
|---|---|
| [Time series and trends](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/time-series.html) | `line_chart()`, `area_chart()`, `stacked_area_chart()`, `area_band()`, `streamgraph()`, `calendar_heatmap()`, `anim_line_chart()` |
| [Comparing categories](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/comparisons.html) | `bar_chart()`, `horz_bar_chart()`, `lollipop_chart()`, `horz_lollipop()`, `dumbbell_chart()`, `slope_chart()`, `bump_chart()`, `waterfall_chart()`, `radar_chart()`, `radial_bar_chart()`, `bar_chart_race()` |
| [Distributions](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/distributions.html) | `histogram()`, `violin_plot()`, `beeswarm_plot()`, `ridgeline_plot()`, `animated_histogram()` |
| [Relationships and flows](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/relationships.html) | `scatter_plot()`, `hexbin_plot()`, `chord_diagram()` |
| [Part-to-whole and hierarchies](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/composition.html) | `pie_chart()`, `treemap_chart()`, `waffle_chart()`, `sunburst_chart()`, `mosaic_chart()`, `rose_chart()`, `parliament_chart()` |
| [KPIs and monitoring](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/kpis.html) | `gauge_chart()`, `bullet_chart()`, `liquid_chart()`, `pulse_grid()` |
| [Playful indicators](https://feddelegrand7.github.io/ddplot/articles/playful.html) | `heart_fill()`, `glass_fill()`, `plant_growth()`, `flame()`, `flower()` |

## Using `ddplot` in Shiny

Every `ddplot` chart is an `r2d3` htmlwidget, so in a `Shiny` app you can use `r2d3::d3Output()` in the UI and `r2d3::renderD3()` in the server. When an input changes, the chart is redrawn in place with the new data and options. Interactive state, such as the zoom of a `line_chart()` or the series hidden from its legend, is kept between updates.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(ddplot)
library(r2d3)

ui <- fluidPage(

  h2("Example ddplot application"),

  selectInput(
    inputId = "colors",
    label = "Point color",
    choices = colors(),
    selected = "springgreen3"
  ),

  sliderInput(
    inputId = "slider",
    label = "Point size",
    min = 1,
    max = 10,
    value = 3
  ),

  d3Output("scatter", height = "450px")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$scatter <- renderD3({
    scatter_plot(
      data = iris,
      x = "Sepal.Length",
      y = "Sepal.Width",
      size = input$slider,
      col = input$colors
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

## Saving a chart

A chart is an htmlwidget, so it can be saved as a standalone HTML file:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
chart <- line_chart(AirPassengers, y = "passengers")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(chart, "airpassengers.html")
```
